correctness.rationale: The exact recurrence \(S'_j=S_j\cup(r+S_{j-1})\) modulo25 follows by partitioning selected positions. Monotone prefix pruning and nondecreasing canonical ordering cover every multiset. Two independent implementations enumerate all 0..11 depths with counts (1,20,210,1540,8855,35700,78700,89100,58350,21600,3900,0). The explicit ten-term avoiding multiset is verified directly. This gives a complete finite proof of equality, not extrapolation.

The closest fully inspected published case covers \(n=4\) only; the variable-length local zero-sum theorem is not an implication. Equivalent-terminology semantic searches and general web exact-phrase searches found no matching prime-five theorem. Full inaccessible original manuscripts leave residual risk.

value.rationale: The prime-five case is the first odd-prime boundary for which the previously proved \(3p-2\) bound fails to meet \(2p+1\) (at \(p=3\) they coincide). The exact minimum resolves an explicitly posed number-theoretic zero-sum conjecture in a natural first open case; full ten-term obstruction count provides a reproducible structural base for inverse questions. This is an exact finite classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
